title: KAUR v PATEL CATERING LIMITED (In Liquidation) and Ors
text:
IN THE EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS AUTHORITY
AUCKLAND
I TE RATONGA AHUMANA TAIMAHI
TĀMAKI MAKAURAU ROHE
[2026] NZERA 523
3393865
BETWEEN JASPREET KAUR
Applicant
AND PATEL CATERING LIMITED
(In Liquidation)
First Respondent
AND CHAITALI PATEL
Second Respondent
AND NIKUNJ PATEL
Third Respondent
Member of Authority: Eleanor Robinson
Representatives: Susanne Lass, advocate for the Applicant
No appearance for the Respondent
Submissions received: 14 July 2026 from the Applicant
None from the Respondent
Determination: 04 August 2026
COSTS DETERMINATION OF THE AUTHORITY
[1] In a determination dated 22 June 2026 (Determination [2026] NZERA 397) the
Applicant, Jaspreet Kaur, was determined to be owed monies by the First Respondent, Patel
Catering Limited (Patel Catering), which is in liquidation. To the extent that Patel Catering
was unable to make the payments ordered to Ms Kaur, the Second Respondent, Chaitali Patel
(Ms Patel) was ordered to make the payments to Ms Kaur.
[2] In that determination costs were reserved in the hope that the parties would be able to
settle this issue between themselves. Unfortunately they have been unable to do so, and Ms
Kaur has filed submissions in support of an application for a contribution to costs.
[3] The matter involved a half day investigation meeting and a short AVL meeting on 5
June 2026.

[4] Ms Lass, on behalf of Ms Kaur, is claiming a contribution to costs in the sum of
$3,450.00.
[5] Ms Lass submits that the costs incurred in preparing for this matter were substantially
greater than would ordinarily be expected for a half day investigation. This was primarily
occasioned by the Respondent failing to provide wages and time records, or other relevant
employment records, which meant Ms Kaur was required to reconstruct her wages calculations
from primary source documents (e.g. bank statements, IRD records, payslips).
Principles
[6] The power of the Authority to award costs arises from Section 15 of Schedule 2 of the
Employment Relations Act 2000 which states:
15 Power to award costs
(1) The Authority may order any party to a matter to pay to any other party
such costs and expenses (including expenses of witnesses) as the
Authority thinks reasonable.
(2) The Authority may apportion any such costs and expenses between the
parties or any of them as it thinks fit, and may at any time vary or alter
any such order in such manner as it thinks reasonable.
Costs Award
[7] Ms Kaur was the successful party and costs normally follow the event.
[8] I accept that Ms Kaur was hindered by the Respondents’ failure to provide the statutory
documents they were required to maintain, and that this involved Ms Kaur in substantially
greater case preparation than is usual. It is also accepted that the detailed preparation and
presentation of her case assisted the Authority.
[9] I find that this justifies the uplift in costs sought.
[10] Patel Catering is ordered to pay Ms Kaur the sum of $3,450.00 as a contribution to
costs, pursuant to clause 15 of Schedule 2 of the Employment Relations Act 2000.
[11] Ms Kaur has also claimed reimbursement of $121.92 in respect of disbursements as
supported by invoices. I accept these disbursements were reasonably incurred.
[12] The First Respondent Patel Catering is ordered to pay Ms Kaur the following
sums:
• $3,450.00 in respect of a contribution to costs.
• $121.92 in respect of disbursements.
• The filing fee of $71.55 in respect of this application

Respondent Ms Patel is ordered to make the payment.
